name: Saturn from Voyager 2, July 10, 1981
blurb: The ringed planet, about 120,500 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 2's narrow-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: Saturn filling much of the frame, fully lit, from about 44 million kilometers away, 47 days before Voyager 2's closest approach to Saturn on August 26, 1981. Its rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock, from dust-sized grains to pieces as big as a house.
